ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: The student’s own self is the self that a questioning student asks the respondent to identify in an encounter.
EvidenceBody: Dasui Fazhen replies that the student’s self is his own and then the student’s own, refusing a stable ownership boundary. Zhaozhou Congshen returns the question to the one recollecting, while another reply asks, “Who else?” Foyan Qingyuan tests Yunmen’s formula against mountains and rivers; Daoqian asks what purpose the question serves, and Kexun places the answer in marketplace or open country.

DraftEvidence.ZenBend: Ordinary possession becomes a live interview test: “own” cannot be settled by a detached definition because the answer shifts with who is asking, answering, and looking at the world.
DraftEvidence.CounterexampleOrLimit: The phrase does not establish a metaphysical self or a doctrine of no-self; the retained answers disagree in form and remain tied to their particular exchanges.

ComparedThings: the same expression in questions, answers, comments, and verdicts
